title: MCP server manager
goal: Configure, start, supervise and stop MCP servers for agents, with explicit trust for project-defined servers, a minimal environment for child processes, and bounded timeouts and output sizes.
scope_in: Config sources: user `<config dir>/mcp.json` and project `.centcom/mcp.json`: `{ servers: { <name>: { type: 'stdio', command: string, args?: string[], env?: Record<string,string>, cwd?: string } | { type: 'http'|'sse', url: string, headers?: Record<string,string> } } }`; server names `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`.

Trust gate: a project-defined server (or any server whose definition hash changed) is not started until `TrustStore.isTrusted('mcp', sha256(canonical JSON of definition))` (store from lane C013); a `needsTrust` list is exposed for the UI to prompt; user-config servers are trusted implicitly.

Lifecycle: lazy start on first use, handshake timeout 15 s, health ping every 30 s, restart with backoff 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... cap 30 s, max 5 consecutive failures then `failed` until manual `restart`; stop with SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3 s on agent/runner exit.

Child environment is an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, TMPDIR) plus declared `env` after `${VAR}` expansion restricted to an allow-list of variable names the user config names in `env_passthrough`; `secret:<name>` values resolved by an injected `SecretResolver` (keychain), never stored in config files.
Tool exposure: tools named `mcp__<server>__<tool>` handed to the runner; call timeout default 60 000 ms, result size cap 256 KiB (truncated with a marker), concurrency cap 4 per server.
URL servers: https only except loopback; no redirects to other origins; headers never logged.
Status API for UI: `{ name, state: 'stopped'|'starting'|'ready'|'failed'|'untrusted', tools: number, lastError?: code }`.
scope_out: Implementing the MCP protocol transport itself beyond using the SDK/official client library (justify the dependency).
Permission decisions for MCP tool calls: lane C015 (this lane only names the tools and marks read-only hints).
build_against: A tiny stdio MCP fixture server (packages/agent/src/mcp/__fixtures__/echo-server.ts) that supports initialize, tools/list, a slow tool, a huge-output tool and a crash-on-call tool; fake clock for timeouts; in-memory TrustStore.
interfaces: `createMcpManager(deps: { fs: McpFs; spawn: SpawnFn; trust: TrustStore; secrets: SecretResolver; clock: Clock; bus: AgentBus; log: Logger; config: McpConfig }): McpManager`

`interface McpManager { load(projectRoot?: string): Promise<{ servers: McpServerStatus[]; needsTrust: PendingTrust[] }>; trust(name: string): Promise<void>; ensureStarted(name: string): Promise<void>; listTools(): Promise<McpToolInfo[]>; callTool(server: string, tool: string, input: unknown, o?: { timeoutMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<McpToolResult>; restart(name: string): Promise<void>; stopAll(): Promise<void>; status(): McpServerStatus[] }`
acceptance: A project `.centcom/mcp.json` server is reported `untrusted` and never spawned (spawn mock call count 0) until `trust(name)`; editing its `args` changes the hash and reverts it to `untrusted`.

Child env for a stdio server contains only the allow-listed variables + declared env: a poisoned parent env with `CENTCOM_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` shows none of them in the spawned env.

Handshake that does not complete in 15 000 ms (fake clock) marks the server `failed` and kills the child; the crash-on-call fixture is restarted with delays 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and after 5 consecutive failures stays `failed`.
A tool returning 1 MiB is truncated to 256 KiB with a trailing marker, and the call result flags `truncated:true`; a slow tool call is aborted at 60 000 ms with `McpTimeout`.
`stopAll` terminates children: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL at 3 s if still alive, resolving in <= 4 s; no zombie child in the process list (test via pid check).
Tool names follow `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; a server named `a__b` or a tool name containing control characters is rejected.
An `http` URL server with scheme `http://example.com` is rejected; `https://` and `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` accepted; a 302 to another origin is not followed.
guardrails: MUST NOT start a project-defined MCP server (it runs an arbitrary command) without explicit local trust bound to the definition hash.
MUST NOT pass the parent environment, tokens or keychain data to servers; secrets only via `secret:` references resolved at spawn.
MUST NOT log commands, args, env, headers, URLs with credentials or tool inputs/outputs.
MUST bound everything: startup 15 s, call 60 s, output 256 KiB, 4 concurrent calls per server, 20 servers total.
MUST NOT shell-interpolate: `command` + `args` are spawned as argv without a shell.
failure_modes: Server binary missing -> status `failed` with `lastError:'spawn_failed'`; other servers unaffected; agent continues without those tools.
Server writes non-protocol noise on stdout -> ignored up to 1 MiB then killed as `protocol_error`.
Trust store corrupted -> treated as empty (everything untrusted).
notes: Trust semantics reuse TrustStore from lane C013. Dependency choice for the MCP client (official SDK) must be justified in the PR (licence MIT, no install scripts).
